rules.title: Excessive Dependents
rules.rule_text: A member enrolling more than 10 dependents under a single supplemental health policy is unusual and warrants investigation. Large dependent counts—especially on wellness or accident plans—may indicate fabricated dependents used to file multiple small claims.
rules.summary: More than 10 dependents under single member triggers BLOCK.
fraud_indicators: Dependent count exceeds 10
Dependents added in rapid succession near open enrollment deadline
Multiple dependents sharing identical address or date of birth ranges
Claims filed for all dependents within short timeframe

rules.title: Rapid Dependent Filing
rules.rule_text: More than 5 dependent claims filed within 30 days under a single member indicates potential claim stacking or fabricated events.
rules.summary: More than 5 dependent claims in 30 days triggers BLOCK.
fraud_indicators: Batch filing of dependent claims on same or consecutive days
All claims for similar amounts or same procedure codes
No prior claims history for these dependents

rules.title: Termination Rush Filing
rules.rule_text: Claims filed within 14 days of an employee's termination date may represent last-opportunity abuse — filing claims for services not rendered before coverage ends.
rules.summary: Claim filed within 14 days of termination triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Claim date falls just before termination effective date
Multiple claims filed in final days of coverage
No prior claims pattern from this member

rules.title: Recent Policy Change
rules.rule_text: Policy ownership or beneficiary changes within 90 days of a claim may indicate manipulation — especially for critical illness or accident indemnity plans.
rules.summary: Policy ownership/beneficiary changed within 90 days of claim triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Beneficiary changed to unrelated party shortly before claim
Policy upgrade to higher tier immediately before large claim
Coverage type changed to match upcoming claim type

rules.title: No Facility Record
rules.rule_text: Accident or hospital indemnity claims that cannot be matched to a facility admission record suggest possible phantom billing or fabricated events.
rules.summary: Accident/hospital claim with no matching facility record triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: No hospital admission found for hospital indemnity claim
ER visit claimed but no emergency department record
Facility named does not exist in provider registry

rules.title: High-Volume Provider
rules.rule_text: Providers submitting more than 50 supplemental health claims in a 90-day window may be operating as a provider mill — generating unnecessary services to drive supplemental payouts.
rules.summary: Provider with >50 supplemental claims in 90 days triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Claim volume far exceeds peer providers in same specialty
Identical procedure codes across many patients
Claims concentrated on wellness exams or routine procedures
Patients traveling unusual distances to this provider

rules.title: Duplicate/Resubmission
rules.rule_text: Claims with the same member, provider, diagnosis code, and amount within 7 days are likely duplicates or deliberate resubmissions to collect double payment.
rules.summary: Duplicate claim within 7 days triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Exact match on member, provider, amount, and diagnosis
Claim resubmitted after initial denial with minor changes
Same service date with different claim IDs

rules.title: Amount Outlier
rules.rule_text: Claim amounts exceeding 3 standard deviations above the mean for that claim type indicate potential upcoding or inflated billing.
rules.summary: Claim amount >3 sigma above mean for type triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Amount far exceeds typical range for procedure/service
Unbundled charges that should be grouped
Add-on charges without corresponding base procedure

rules.title: Early Tenure Claim
rules.rule_text: Claims filed within the first 60 days of coverage enrollment may indicate pre-existing utilization or enrollment motivated by planned claims.
rules.summary: Claim within 60 days of enrollment start triggers INFO.
fraud_indicators: Member enrolled and filed claim almost immediately
Large claim amount in first policy month
Critical illness diagnosis within waiting period

rules.title: Shared Address
rules.rule_text: Multiple unrelated members filing claims from the same address may indicate a dependent ring or organized scheme using a single location as a front.
rules.summary: 3+ unrelated members at same address triggers INFO.
fraud_indicators: Multiple member IDs registered at identical address
Members not listed as dependents of each other
Address is commercial or PO Box rather than residential

rules.title: Surgical/Emergency Mismatch
rules.rule_text: Claims categorized as surgical or emergency that lack corresponding clinical evidence (operative notes, ER triage records) may indicate fabricated severity to increase payout.
rules.summary: Surgical/emergency claim without supporting clinical records triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: No operative report for surgical claim
No ER triage documentation for emergency claim
Procedure code inconsistent with diagnosis

rules.title: Excessive Contact Attempts
rules.rule_text: More than 5 failed contact attempts with a claimant may indicate avoidance behavior, which is correlated with fraudulent claims.
rules.summary: More than 5 failed contact attempts triggers INFO.
fraud_indicators: Member unreachable at all listed phone numbers
Returned mail at address on file
Voicemail full or disconnected

rules.title: Disability Portal Critical Illness
rules.rule_text: When a critical illness claim cross-references with an active disability claim for the same member, additional scrutiny is warranted to ensure claims are not duplicative across benefit lines.
rules.summary: Cross-reference with disability portal for critical illness claims triggers INFO.
fraud_indicators: Active STD/LTD claim for same diagnosis period
Disability and supplemental claims filed same week
Different diagnosis codes for overlapping conditions

rules.title: Suspicious Banner Active
rules.rule_text: A suspicious_banner flag already exists on the member record in Prudential 360, indicating prior SIU involvement or prior fraud alerts. All new claims should receive elevated scrutiny.
rules.summary: Existing suspicious_banner on member record triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: Prior SIU investigation on this member
Previous claim denial for fraud
Active watchlist entry

rules.title: Family Claim Cluster
rules.rule_text: When a member and 3+ dependents all file claims within 60 days, it may indicate coordinated filing — legitimate for a real family event, but a red flag when combined with other indicators.
rules.summary: Member + 3 dependents filing within 60 days triggers FLAG.
fraud_indicators: All family members claiming same or similar conditions
Claims filed in batch on same day
Dependent ages inconsistent with family structure

DEPENDENT_ABUSE.description: Fabricated or inflated dependent enrollment to generate multiple claim payouts
DEPENDENT_ABUSE.action: Block auto-adjudication, SIU referral, verify dependent eligibility via Prudential 360

AUTO_ADJ_GAMING.description: Structuring claims to stay below auto-adjudication thresholds and avoid review
indicators: Claims clustered just below threshold amounts
AUTO_ADJ_GAMING.action: Flag provider, lower auto-adj threshold for provider, CBR review

DOCUMENT_TAMPERING.description: Altered or fabricated medical documents submitted to support claims
indicators: Missing metadata or headers on documents
DOCUMENT_TAMPERING.action: PMR hold, request original records from facility, SIU referral

POLICY_MANIPULATION.description: Beneficiary or coverage changes timed to coincide with large claims
POLICY_MANIPULATION.action: Review policy change history in FIS/PAS, verify coverage dates, escalate if pattern confirmed

PROVIDER_MILL.description: Provider generating excessive supplemental health claims via unnecessary services
PROVIDER_MILL.action: Provider audit, cross-reference with state medical board, block new claims from provider
